correctness.rationale: Uniform labeled double-occurrence words project to uniform induced 3- and 4-label subwords. Exhaustive small-word enumeration gives the exact rational 3-label and 4-label probabilities; the number of same-third-chord and different-third-chord terms is exactly n-2 and (n-2)(n-3). Summation yields both claimed closed forms for all integers n>=2 and determines every sign, including n=2. The small cases certify local constants and are not extrapolated as a global finite experiment.

originality.rationale: The published chord-diagram results inspected concern the marginal degree (Acan) or aggregate crossing counts/normal approximation (Paguyo) and their extensions to embedded graphs (Arenas-Velilla–Arizmendi), whereas the present statement conditions on the mutual adjacency status of two marked chords and gives both exact finite covariance branches and a sharp nonedge sign change. Existing total-crossing moments and short-chord covariance formulas likewise do not imply the branch decomposition. These comparisons are by statement and implication, not merely titles; an implicit prior identity remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: An older full joint two-vertex law for random circle graphs might contain this special covariance, possibly under degree-assortativity terminology.
Prior work can imply the unconditional positive covariance, and no novelty is claimed for that aggregate.

value.rationale: Edge/nonedge assortativity is a natural graph-level dependence statistic in the classical uniform circle graph. The theorem proves a sharply located qualitative reversal for nonadjacent chords, despite the unconditional degree covariance staying positive, while the crossing-conditioned branch remains positive. The branch distinction is mathematically invisible to aggregate crossing moments and motivates separate edge and nonedge correlation analyses.
